html:
SMTO-TSK-0013 — The previous task is still finishing

GUID: c93cb054-b06e-40cc-93e3-e30ea625b897
Slug: task-settling
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • A task in this conversation is still running, stopping or paused, so SMTO didn't start your new request. SMTO can't tell from this message alone whether your earlier click already took effect.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the conversation without clicking anything else. Check whether your message already appears, or is waiting in the Queued list just above the message box. Your earlier request may already have been accepted, and sending it again would make the Agent do the work twice.
  2. Wait until the current task shows it has finished or Stopped. If it shows Paused, choose Resume to finish it, or Stop current task if you no longer need it. A conversation runs one task at a time, so the earlier one must end first.
  3. Reload the page, and only if your request isn't already shown or queued, send it again. Once the earlier task has ended, SMTO can safely start your new one.

What success looks like

  • The earlier task shows as finished or stopped, and your new request appears once in the conversation and starts.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. If the task seems stuck in Stopping for a long time, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't click Send repeatedly.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The conversation still has prior work that is active, stopping, paused, waiting or owned (or a continuation, fork, resume or queued successor is already in progress), so the new submission or control was refused.

What this means

  • Prior work is active, stopping, waiting or still owned, or a continuation/fork/submission cannot pass the conversation's transition and capacity checks. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Prior work is active, stopping, waiting or still owned, or a continuation/fork/submission cannot pass the conversation's transition and capacity checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current task, live future, owner and cancellation state instead of submitting the same work again.

How to fix it

  • A predecessor or task-lane owner is still non-terminal, or a continuation/resume is already scheduled for this run. Inspect the conversation's current task state and queue before acting; wait for the transition to settle, then refresh and use the control the current state offers. Do not submit a duplicate execution request.
  • Wait for the current transition to settle, then refresh its authoritative state and controls. Do not submit a duplicate execution request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing transitions settle and current controls permit the intended next action.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
